source: The amazing digital circus role play game where you can morph into any character you want from tadc and there's a vip room and the vip room costs 1000 dollars in the game NOT ROBUX and I have infinite dollars

image_prompt.text: A central circus ring as the oversized gathering core, sized for a crowd of morphed players without traffic jams
A big top visible from anywhere in the map so players can navigate by sight
Composed circus backdrops - banners, lights, painted tents - built for screenshots and roleplay scenes
A VIP room players go inside, decorated apart from the main floor
colourful circus tents and interactive props around the ring
morph stations around the main area where a player changes into a character

layout_placement.text: the VIP room as a restricted volume, entry gated on an in-game currency purchase

notes: Static settlement carries no personal property, which fits: personalisation here happens entirely through the morph, never through a house.
The VIP room makes this P3 - it is an interior space entered from the main floor.
The price - 1000 in-game dollars, explicitly not Robux - and the users own infinite balance are economy facts the handoff cannot carry.
Morphing into named characters from an existing IP is a character-asset question, not a layout one.

open_questions.ask: Is this one circus tent and its surroundings, or a whole fairground you walk between attractions in?

answers.ask: Is this one circus tent and its surroundings, or a whole fairground you walk between attractions in?
answers.answer: Make it one main circus tent with a small surrounding entrance area, so the roleplay map stays focused and playable.

answers.ask: Should the main area be indoors under the big top, or an open outdoor fairground?
answers.answer: The main area should be indoors under the big top, matching The Amazing Digital Circus setting.

answers.ask: Besides morphing and hanging out, is there anything to do - shows, minigames, roleplay scenes?
answers.answer: The prompt only calls for morphing and hanging out, so keep it as a simple roleplay space with no extra shows or minigames.
